subject: body
title: Fruits and Vegetables
about: Eating a rainbow and what each color does (red for the heart, orange for the eyes, green for bones, blue and purple for the brain, white for the germ fighters), vitamins and apple-skin fiber, why fresh, frozen, canned and dried all count and raw or cooked both count, fruit for something sweet, telling a fruit from a vegetable (with the tomato as the tricky one in a note), where strawberries grow, seeds, cutting grapes small for little kids, and the five-a-day idea. NC 1.NPA.1.2 (a variety of foods and why we eat them) and 1.NPA.1.3 (where foods come from); goes deeper than the Food Groups sorting level in Healthy Me. Read it together and hunt for each color in the fridge.
tip: At the store, let him pick one fruit or vegetable of a color you did not eat this week.

cards.q: Why do we eat fruits and vegetables of every color?
cards.note: Red, orange, green, purple and white foods each carry different helpers for your body.

cards.q: Red foods like strawberries and tomatoes help which part of you stay strong?
cards.note: Red fruits and vegetables carry helpers that are good for your heart and blood.

cards.q: Orange foods like carrots and sweet potatoes help keep which part of you healthy?
cards.note: Your body turns the orange color helper into vitamin A, which your eyes need to stay healthy. Carrots do not give you super night vision, though.

cards.q: Green foods like broccoli and spinach help build strong...?
cards.note: Green vegetables carry calcium and vitamin K, two helpers that make bones hard and strong.

cards.q: Blue and purple foods like grapes and plums help which thinking part of you?
cards.note: Blueberries, grapes, plums and eggplant carry helpers that are good for your brain and memory.

cards.q: White foods like bananas, cauliflower and onions help your body do what?
cards.note: White counts as a rainbow color too. Garlic, onions, mushrooms and bananas help your germ fighters.

cards.q: Fruits and vegetables are full of tiny helpers for your eyes, skin and germ fighters. What are they?
cards.note: Vitamins are too small to see. Your body cannot make most of them, so you eat them.

cards.q: Carrots can be raw and crunchy or cooked and soft. Which way counts as a vegetable?
cards.note: Raw, cooked, frozen or canned, a vegetable is a vegetable. Cooking changes the texture, and some kids like one way better than the other.

cards.q: A raisin is a dried fruit. What was it before it dried out?
cards.note: Raisins are grapes dried in the sun. Dried fruit counts as fruit too, so raisins in your lunchbox are a fruit.

cards.q: Fresh, frozen or canned. Which fruits and vegetables count?
cards.note: Frozen peas and canned peaches count just like fresh ones. Pick canned fruit packed in juice or water.

cards.q: You want something sweet after dinner. Which sweet food is an everyday food?
cards.note: Fruit is nature's dessert. Its sugar comes with vitamins, fiber and water.

cards.q: Fruits grow from a flower and hold seeds inside. Which one is a fruit?
cards.note: A peach grows from a blossom and has a pit, a big seed, inside, while carrots and potatoes grow under the ground. Tricky one: a tomato has seeds too, so scientists call it a fruit, but at mealtime it counts as a vegetable.

cards.q: Carrots are roots and lettuce is leaves. What do we call plant roots, stems and leaves we eat?
cards.note: Broccoli is a flower bud, celery is a stem, spinach is leaves. All vegetables.

cards.q: Apples grow high on trees. Where do strawberries grow?
cards.note: Strawberries grow on small plants close to the ground. In North Carolina you can pick them at a farm in spring.

cards.q: Whole grapes are round and can get stuck in a little kid's throat. What does a grown-up do first?
cards.note: Round, slippery foods like whole grapes, cherry tomatoes and hot dog pieces get cut small for little kids. Sit down and chew well too.

cards.q: About how many handfuls of fruits and vegetables should you eat each day?
cards.note: Five a day: a fruit or veggie at every meal and every snack adds up fast.

cards.q: Which fruit can you eat with the skin on for extra fiber?
cards.note: Apple, pear and potato skins have lots of fiber. Wash well and crunch away.

cards.q: What is inside most fruits that can grow into a new plant?
cards.note: Apple seeds, peach pits and watermelon seeds can all grow into new plants. Fruit comes from plants.
